newsitem.title: USA: Seagull CEO comfortable with EPS consensus.
newsitem.headline: Seagull CEO comfortable with EPS consensus.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Barry Galt said he was comfortable with analysts' consensus estimates of $0.18 a share earnings in the fourth quarter and $0.44 a share earnings for the year before charges.
He said the Houston-based oil and natural gas exploration and production company expected to charge $8 million to $10 million in acquisition costs against fourth quarter earnings.

Seagull recently purchased 100 percent of two Egyptian concessions from Exxon Corp units for $74 million and merged with Global Natural Resources in a stock transaction that added prospects in Egypt and the Ivory Coast.

The two deals boosted shareholder equity by nearly 30 percent and raised cash flow and market capitalization by about 75 percent. The company expects its oil production to double in 1997 as a result of the acquisitions and is drafting a $250 million capital budget for international and domestic exploration and production, Galt said in a speech to a Houston business group on Tuesday.
